messages:
ana: FYI noticed a ~18-22% p95 spike in the nightly canary after merge rwl/pr-4123.
mike: ugh, saw that in CI perf dashboard too. was that the autotune weight change PR?
sophia: yeah PR-4123 lowered the compile-priority weight from 0.7 -> 0.45 for short seqs to prefer cached kernels.
kai: I pushed a quick flamegraph from the canary: a lot of tiny JIT compiles running concurrently, compile queue saturated.
ana: (typo) ana: re: flamegraph — can you paste the top stacks? curious which kernel paths are toggling.
ana: sorry ignore prev.
ana: ana: here's the snippet from /var/log/runtime/compiles.log (truncated):
```
[2071234510] compile:start model=redwood-tiny seq=8 backend=cu110 kernel=attn_v2 id=0x9f
[2071234510] cache:miss key=attn_v2_seq8_opt
[2071234512] compile:start model=redwood-tiny seq=12 backend=cu110 kernel=attn_v1 id=0xA3
[2071234513] compile:finish id=0x9f time_ms=48
[2071234514] compile:start model=redwood-tiny seq=8 backend=cu110 kernel=attn_v2 id=0xC1
[2071234514] compile:start model=redwood-tiny seq=8 backend=cu110 kernel=attn_v1 id=0xC2
[2071234515] compile:queue-depth 32
```
sophia: that pattern (v2 vs v1 alternating) screams heuristic oscillation — we're reselecting kernels per batch because priority score is too close.
mike: I reproduced locally with short-batch synthetic load (batch size 1-2). enabling the old weight removes the oscillation.
lucas: does the KV cache get invalidated between those requests? maybe we purge based on seq heuristics.
kai: checked KV eviction logs — no explicit eviction. it's not invalidation, it's selection flip causing new compiles because different kernel keys.
sophia: hypothesis: lowering weight gave compiles higher chance to prefer cached but the tie-breaking introduced pseudo-randomness across workers, so different workers pick different kernels and miss shared cache.
ana: (again typo) ana: is this only short seq? any effect on longseq traffic?
ana: ana: longseq looks fine, short sequences dominate nightly canary workload.
mike: can we reproduce a compile storm in CI e2e? I can make a small harness to simulate 200 qps of shortseqs.
ana: ana: please try. if we can trigger in CI that will justify a rollback hold.
deploy-bot: deploy job started for canary rwl/pr-4123 @ 2071234520
lucas: added perf test to reproduce, sending link: https://ci.internal/job/shortseq-compile-repro/207
sophia: while you run that, suggestion: temporary mitigation - increase hysteresis on selector or restore previous weight. which is faster to ship?
kai: revert is fastest. adding a toggle in runtime config to set selector weight per cluster is medium work.
mike: agree revert. can also add a canary gate in rollout to block if compile rate > X.
ana: ana: opened rollback PR rwl/pr-4130, reverts the weight change. it's small.
ana: ana: also created issue PERF-785 to track a safer fix (selector lockstep + deterministic tie-breaker + per-worker affinity for cache coherency).
sophia: perf test finished: compile starts peaked at 4200/min during the run, typical baseline is ~80/min.
ana: :eyes: that's a 52x compile delta.
lucas: adding a temporary alert on compile-rate for canaries.
mike: I'll hold the main rollout and trigger a revert deploy.
deploy-bot: deploy rwl/pr-4130 (rollback) queued @ 2071234590
ana: followups:
- rollback now
- bisect to find if earlier churn primed caches (maybe older kernel keys changed)
- add deterministic tiebreaker to selector (e.g., consistent-hash on model+seq) in PERF-785
kai: I'll start a bisect job across commits around PR-4123 to see if anything else contributes.
sophia: also add metrics for "selector-flips-per-session" and expose per-worker compile-key distribution.
lucas: thanks team. temporary hold on any autotune weight changes until PERF-785 is done.
mike: noted. will update rollout doc + send heads-up to product.
ana: thanks all. :thumbsup:
